einstellungen.text: You're counting yellow cards. And you miss your best friend.
In three days, you open the school exhibition.
The topic: perception. Together with Eda. And you don't want to make a single mistake. Not one.
Dress rehearsal in the screening room. The curtains are closed. The projector blows warm air in your face.
Cards fly across the screen. Your job: count every yellow one.
Click. Click. Click. You count out loud. Twelve. No mistakes.
"Twelve. Nice. Did you see anything else?"
Eda. Your best friend. Since fifth grade.
You shake your head. There was nothing but cards.
Ms. Sen, your teacher, rewinds the recording. She smiles kind of funny. Like she knows something.
In nineteen ninety-nine, two researchers showed it: when you focus on one thing, you can miss something unexpected.
Second forty-one. At the edge of the frame, someone raises a hand.
It's Eda. She's waving. She's pointing at her page. She needs help.
Your face goes hot. You were looking the whole time. And you still saw nothing.
Ms. Sen asks if you want to cut that moment out. You say, "It stays in."
Then the recording keeps playing. Eda was standing right next to you the whole time.
